title: Exploring the Unfairness of DP-SGD Across Settings
benchmark_measurement: Fairness (specifically, F1 scores and δ-Unequal Risk) of toxicity detection models across different demographic groups, including religious groups (Christian, Muslim, other religions).
findings: Baseline toxicity detection models showed significant performance disparities across groups, with the lowest F1 scores for minority religious groups and Christians. The study found a negative, logarithmic correlation between privacy (enforced by DP-SGD) and fairness (δ-Unequal Risk), meaning that as models become more private, they become less fair. This trade-off holds across different settings and affects all demographic subgroups, including the religious ones.
